what_is_unconditional_vs_ruling_conditio.why: AdmissibleRoots proves admissible <=> y_(1^3) = 0 <=> z in {q, z_D}. That is a theorem ABOUT the condition. That the DECAY channel must satisfy it is settled by the 2026-08-15 owner ruling (convention D), and the trace-convention registry explicitly preserves the prior analysis: 'superseded AS A STATUS, NOT AS ANALYSIS: its finding that neither convention was DERIVED for this channel stands'. MarkovZFullBarCondition's own docstring says the same -- 'Which horn is the decay channel's is NOT decided here: no corpus block derives the decay fibre'. So the block is a RULING, not a proved impossibility.
what_is_unconditional_vs_ruling_conditio.consequence_for_the_open_problem: The D re-derivation is not blocked by an impossibility. The decay trace is one affine scalar; the data fixes it exactly at z = 0.99850; the ruling fixes it at z_D = 0.61269. Closing the gap means DERIVING THE DECAY FIBRE -- which the registry names as the open item -- not finding another correction. The thing missing is not a form.
